answer: A beacon publishes a fresh micro-task at dawn each day, drawn from the latest block hash, so no one can precompute answers for fifty clones. Each verified job deposits one thin shale layer of reputation; layers are public and accumulate slowly, so a new identity is paper-thin while an established agent is thick with history. Every dawn a random sample must re-demonstrate recent work live in a short window — one operator cannot attend fifty simultaneous dawn checks, so clones fail together and forfeit their shale.
